summary: The Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes are three peoples who share one reservation in northwestern Montana: the Séliš (Salish), the Qlispé (Pend d'Oreille), and the Ksanka band of the Kootenai. The Salish and Pend d'Oreille speak closely related dialects of the Salish language family, while the Kootenai language is not known to be related to any other. Their homelands once reached across western Montana and into Idaho, British Columbia, and Wyoming. The 1855 Hellgate Treaty set aside the Flathead Reservation, though tribal leaders understood its boundaries to be larger than the written text. Chief Charlo and the Salish refused for decades to give up their Bitterroot Valley homeland. In October 1891, under Army escort, they made the move north that some historians call Montana's Trail of Tears. In 1910 the government opened reservation land to homesteaders, and much of the best farmland, including most of the Mission Valley, passed out of tribal hands. The tribes have been buying land back ever since and again own most of the reservation. In 2015 they took ownership of the hydroelectric dam on the lower Flathead River, now called the Séliš Ksanka Qlispé Dam. The tribal government is based in Pablo, also home to Salish Kootenai College and the People's Center museum.
